observation.visible_scene: Five thin, slightly tilted sticks (each with a short red band near its upper end) stand against a pure black background. From the tip of each stick a translucent blue-white smoke plume rises, initially as separate, fairly smooth columns leaning toward the upper-left of the frame. The sticks themselves keep constant positions and angles throughout.
visible_changes: The smoke continuously rises from the fixed tips and drifts upward/leftward, so the plumes lengthen and shift within the frame while their bases stay anchored at the stick tips.

The initially distinct, laminar-looking streams progressively deform and intertwine: the plumes from the middle and right sticks merge into a broader, wavy, turbulent mass in the upper portion of the frame, while the leftmost stream remains comparatively coherent but also undulates.
The overall smoke pattern becomes more billowy and folded over time (clearly by the later frames), showing shape change (turbulent deformation) rather than rigid translation of a single object.
No change is visible in the sticks, their red bands, or the black background.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the incense was lit and the airflow conditions before t=0.
Whether the smoke would eventually dissipate or the sticks burn down after the excerpt ends.
The cause of the lateral drift (draft vs. buoyancy).
uncertain_details: Camera motion cannot be judged because the background is uniform black with no fixed reference; the scene is treated as a static camera with the smoke as the moving element.
Whether the merging of plumes is true mixing or partly a visual overlap of separate streams is not fully resolvable from the frames.
